@@ -7,6 +7,17 @@ description: Guide and reference for driving CamCraft headlessly via its Model C
 
 CamCraft exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on stdio (`camcraft-cli mcp`, #128), allowing an AI agent to drive a complete CAM programming session headlessly: importing models, defining setups and stock, selecting tools, creating and editing operations, selecting geometric features, simulating/verifying, and posting NC programs.
 
+## Live MCP idle window
+
+Start `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7777 --mcp-idle-timeout 1800` to allow
+1800 seconds without a complete request line. The default is 300 seconds.
+`CAMCRAFT_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT` is the environment fallback; the option wins.
+Use non-negative whole seconds that fit `u64`. Zero disables idle expiry
+for live TCP clients and authenticated UI link clients. It does not disable
+the UI link's five-second hello deadline or the line limits.
+Set the option on the app, not on `camcraft-cli mcp --connect`.
+The stdio bridge does not reconnect automatically after a drop.
+
 ## Architecture & Principles
 
 - **Transport & Protocol:** Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdio (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`).

+# Branch writers and PR reviewers (#3661)
+
+This is a cooperative ownership guard, not an atomic distributed lock.
+GitHub comments are the shared record. A local file cannot coordinate two
+machines. Read this procedure before dispatch, before local work without a
+worker, and immediately before a push. AGENTS.md and
+[issue-claims](../SKILL.md) still govern claim lifetimes, withdrawals and
+refresh timing. Ownership grants no new push, review or merge permission.
+
+## Record and read
+
+Use the upstream issue thread for the canonical writer record. Extend the
+normal `claimed:` comment; do not create a second issue claim for a worker
+already dispatched under it. The dispatcher writes the record on behalf of
+one named worker, then passes its URL. The worker confirms that same record.
+A self-started worker performs the dispatcher steps itself. It posts one
+claim with its writer record only when a new claim is needed. For a live
+claim of the same claimant, link the new writer record to that claim after
+the previous writer releases. A writer record must come from the claimant
+or its verified dispatcher and name that claimant's worker. Another
+account's unsupported record cannot replace or extend the claim.
+A coordinator is not a second writer and must not push the worker's commits.
+
+Use the upstream PR thread for the canonical review record, including a
+delta review. Link the issue's writer record from the PR when it exists.
+Before a PR exists, use the issue only. If a PR has no issue, put its writer
+record on the PR. Search other PRs with the same head repository and branch;
+the writer scope is the branch, not a PR number. Read their records too.
+
+Only collaborator-authored reviewer records count, as in AGENTS.md
+"Only collaborators' reviews count". Verify both the record author and the
+reviewer's GitHub login against the base repository's collaborators with
+`permissions.push` (use the paginated collaborator API from AGENTS.md).
+The dispatcher must use a collaborator account to post a counted review
+record. A fork owner is not a base collaborator by owning the fork.
+A contributor pre-check uses no reviewer record, no counted review marker
+and no review labels. A known non-collaborator record does not block a
+collaborator review, whatever its stated role or age. Failed authority
+reads mean STOP; do not infer collaborator status from a marker or label.
+
+Read the complete threads, not only the latest comment or search snippets:
+
+```bash
+gh api --paginate repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/ISSUE/comments
+gh api --paginate repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/PR/comments
+gh pr view PR --repo NeoTech/Camcraft --json headRefOid,headRefName,headRepository,baseRefName,baseRefOid,state,isDraft
+git ls-remote HEAD_REPOSITORY_URL refs/heads/BRANCH
+```
+
+Replace the uppercase tokens with the exact issue, PR, repository URL and
+branch. Skip the PR reads only when no PR exists. Read the issue labels,
+assignment and claim history as well. Failed or incomplete reads mean STOP,
+not "no owner". A branch read succeeds with no matching ref only when the
+branch is absent; an API 404 does not prove absence.
+
+Append this block to the writer's claim or to a PR review comment. Do not
+use `claimed:` for a review; it must not change the issue claim.
+
+```text
+<!-- ownership: writer | reviewer -->
+Owner: <GitHub login / session / unique worker identity>
+Dispatcher: <GitHub login / session>
+Issue: <upstream issue URL, or none>
+PR: <upstream PR URL, or not yet open>
+Branch: <head repository owner/name> <exact branch>
+Base: <base repository owner/name> <base ref> <full exact SHA>
+Starting head: <full exact SHA>
+Expected remote: <full exact SHA, or absent>
+Started: <UTC ISO time>
+State: active
+```
+
+Choose exactly one role in the marker. For a new branch, `Starting head` is
+the local base commit and `Expected remote` is `absent`. Otherwise both name
+the fetched branch head. Never substitute a short SHA, branch name or
+`FETCH_HEAD` for an exact SHA. Use a unique worker identity even when two
+agents share one GitHub account. Record the actual PR head and base, not an
+assumed `main`. Review ownership is PR-wide, not just per head.
+
+## Before dispatch
+
+1. Read the issue claim and all applicable ownership records. Use
+   issue-claims to decide whether the issue claim is live or ended. Apply
+   the author checks above before treating a record as an owner.
+2. A live writer means stand down and name the owner and record URL.
+   A live reviewer means stand down and name the owner and record URL.
+   Do not dispatch a writer during a review, or a reviewer during writing.
+   The already named worker may resume its own active record; another agent
+   under the same account may not.
+3. If free, append the record. Read it back by its comment URL. Re-read the
+   threads and remote head after posting and before dispatch. Confirm the
+   expected head and sole owner. Pass the record URL, base and starting
+   exact head to the worker. If two active records appear, both sessions
+   STOP until one owner explicitly releases. Do not select a winner by
+   comment order or overwrite another record.
+4. The worker repeats the reads before it edits or reviews. A missing or
+   mismatched record means STOP. No record from an older process is not
+   permission to ignore an existing live claim: name that claimant and stop.
+
+Writer liveness follows the existing issue claim rules: 4 hours for an
+owner-account agent and the three 48-hour activity tests for a contributor.
+These are the only activity tests; there is no writer-specific timeout.
+
+| Contributor claim evidence (not withdrawn or released) | Liveness |
+|---|---|
+| Claimant has an open PR for the issue | Live |
+| Claimant's branch has a commit in the last 48 hours | Live |
+| Claimant commented on the issue in the last 48 hours | Live |
+| All three absent | Stale; follow issue-claims release steps |
+| Withdrawn or released, even with recent activity or an open PR | Ended; only a new claim can start again |
+
+An ended claim stays ended; later activity cannot revive it. A new writer
+needs a new claim after a claim ends. Releasing writer ownership after a
+push does not release the issue claim; the same claimant can record its
+next review-fix worker without reclaiming against itself. A different
+claimant must still stand down while that issue claim is live.
+A released writer record stays released even while its issue claim is live.
+An unreleased writer record cannot outlive an ended or stale issue claim.
+
+A counted review record remains active until its owner posts a result or
+release. It has no expiry timer. Age alone does not release a running review.
+If a counted review appears abandoned, confirm failure with its dispatcher.
+If failure cannot be confirmed, STOP and name the owner; the owner or
+maintainer must release it. Append the confirmed failure and release before
+a replacement record. Keep `.claude/pr-review.lock` and its existing
+one-review rule, including its local stale-lock checks. A free local lock
+does not release a counted public owner.
+
+## Immediately before a push
+
+For a refresh, run at least `cargo check --tests -p <affected-package>` for
+each affected code package, including incoming base changes. A clean merge,
+SAME classification or zero-step quick plan does not replace compilation.
+For shared inputs, including `Cargo.lock`, check each affected package one
+package at a time with `-p`; never `--workspace` or an unqualified
+full-workspace build.
+Record prose-only scope when no code is affected.
+
+Finish the refresh compile check and targeted tests on the final committed
+tree first. Any later tree change invalidates those results. Then do the
+final owner and remote reads below without a build or edit between them
+and the push.
+
+1. Re-read the public owner and claim records and the PR head. Confirm that
+   you are still the sole writer and that no reviewer is active.
+2. Read the exact remote branch with `git ls-remote` again. It must equal
+   `Expected remote` in your active record (or still be absent for the first
+   push). If the remote head moved, STOP. Report the expected and observed
+   SHAs, owner URL and saved local head. Do not merge that unexpected head
+   and retry. Never force-push, including `--force-with-lease`.
+3. Push plainly to the recorded repository and branch. A rejected push is
+   STOP. Preserve the worktree and local commits; report the rejection.
+   Do not retry by rebasing, resetting, deleting or force-pushing.
+4. Read the remote exact head and PR back. Confirm that both equal your
+   local published head. Append a progress comment referencing the owner
+   URL with `Published head: <full SHA>` and `Expected remote: <full SHA>`.
+   That verified progress updates the expected remote for this owner only.
+   If confirmation fails, STOP; do not announce success or dispatch review.
+
+Before posting a review or changing its labels, re-read the records and PR
+head. If the head moved, STOP without a verdict for the new head. Preserve
+findings for the reviewed SHA; release the record before a fresh dispatch.
+
+## Release and handoff
+
+Append a comment referencing the exact owner record URL:
+
+```text
+Ownership released: <record URL>
+Role: <writer or reviewer>
+Owner: <same unique identity>
+Final head: <full SHA>
+Result: <published PR/review URL, or stopped with reason and saved work>
+```
+
+The named owner or maintainer releases the record. A dispatcher may record
+its worker's completion only with a verified result or confirmed failure.
+Do not edit or delete another owner's comment. Release on completion,
+withdrawal or confirmed failure, including when escalation stops work.
+Handoff requires release, fresh reads and a new named owner record. An issue
+claim release uses the existing issue-claims texts separately.
+
+## Guarantee and limits
+
+The guard makes ownership and the expected head visible to cooperating
+sessions. It requires stand-down on observed conflicts and moved heads.
+It cannot serialize simultaneous GitHub comment writes or make a read and
+push atomic. A competing write after the last read can still race. Git's
+plain push rejects non-fast-forward updates; it is not an exact-head lease
+and can accept a fast-forward after a race. Never describe this procedure
+as race-free exclusion. No daemon, service or new dependency is required.
+
+Contract checks pin the dispatch actors and skill links, required record fields, stop
+instructions, lifecycle rules and refresh compilation. They test the
+published procedure, not execution by an agent or distributed exclusion.
+
+| Observed case | Required action |
+|---|---|
+| Live issue claimant, no owner block yet | Stand down; name the claimant |
+| Live writer in another session | Stand down; name the writer |
+| Live counted PR reviewer, same or different head | Stand down; name the reviewer |
+| Known non-collaborator reviewer record | Does not block; contributor pre-checks claim no reviewer ownership |
+| Withdrawn or stale issue claim | Follow issue-claims; only a new claim can start ownership |
+| Writer released, issue claim still live | Same claimant can name its next worker; others stand down |
+| Two active records after readback | Both stop; require explicit release |
+| Remote moved, even if the local tip contains it | Stop; preserve local work; never force |
+| Rejected push | Stop; preserve local work; never force |
+| Clean refresh with affected code | Compile and test before push |
+| Failed or incomplete owner/head read | Stop; do not infer that it is free |

+---
+name: repro-first
+description: Demonstrate a reported CamCraft bug through MCP or a pinning test on current main before fixing it. Preserve the before reading for the PR, and stop with issue evidence when the bug does not reproduce or reproduction is unsupported.
+---
+
+# repro-first - measure the bug before changing its cause
+
+Use this skill before a bug fix, including a takeover or review fix.
+Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), [gh-issues](../gh-issues/SKILL.md),
+[work-issue](../work-issue/SKILL.md) and the
+[ownership guard](../issue-claims/references/ownership.md).
+AGENTS.md takes precedence. Reproduction is not permission to change an
+unclaimed issue or a branch that another writer or reviewer owns.
+
+## 1. Establish the baseline
+
+1. Read the full issue and comments. Identify the input, steps, expected
+   result and observed result. Search for an existing fix or duplicate PR.
+   Check the claim, ownership, effort and release-cut prerequisites in
+   `work-issue` before edits. Record the current process rules.
+2. Fetch the canonical repository's latest `main`. Record its full SHA.
+   In a fork, follow [fork-sync](../fork-sync/SKILL.md): this check does not
+   merge upstream `main` into the fork's `main` or refresh an existing PR.
+   Use an isolated worktree at the recorded upstream commit if necessary.
+   Never switch or pull a checkout that is running a gate.
+3. Keep the implementation unchanged while collecting the before reading.
+   Record the operating system, build command, binary provenance and
+   relevant feature flags. Do not use an old binary as evidence for the
+   fetched `main`. Keep user data private; prefer a small original fixture.
+4. For a takeover, also record the PR's exact starting head. A failure only
+   on that branch is not a reproduced bug on current `main`. Report the
+   distinction; do not refresh the branch merely to obtain a baseline.
+
+## 2. Reproduce before writing the fix
+
+Choose the smallest supported route:
+
+- **MCP:** load [camcraft-mcp](../camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md). Use the shipped
+  tools to create or open the minimal document and run the reported steps.
+  Save the requests, actual responses, diagnostic or numeric reading, and
+  expected result. The binary must come from the recorded baseline.
+  A server connection or screenshot alone does not demonstrate the bug.
+- **Pinning test:** add a focused assertion in an existing domain directory
+  suite, in the lowest crate that provides its imports. Load
+  [gate](../gate/SKILL.md). Run the named test against the unchanged baseline
+  implementation and save its actual failure. The failure must assert the
+  reported behaviour, not a build error, missing fixture or service outage.
+
+Do not start the implementation fix until one route demonstrates the bug.
+For either route, record the input and exact command so another contributor
+can repeat it. Use only permitted clean-room inputs. Do not run generated
+G-code on machinery as part of this software procedure.
+
+### Outcomes that are not a reproduced bug
+
+| Observation | Action |
+|---|---|
+| Current `main` gives the expected result | Stop the fix. Post the SHA, input, command, expected result and actual reading on the issue. Ask for the missing case through that evidence; do not invent a failure or close the issue. |
+| The build fails, MCP lacks the required operation, or the fixture is unavailable | State that reproduction is unsupported or blocked, not that the bug is absent. Post the limitation and partial evidence on the issue. Stop until a supported test or input is available. |
+| The issue changes prose only | Demonstrate the missing or incorrect text and run focused documentation checks. Mark runtime reproduction not applicable. Do not claim that MCP or a regression test failed. |
+| A known-fail test already records the defect | Run that exact test and confirm the expected assertion fails on the baseline. An ignored test that was never run is not evidence. |
+
+A new test committed red on purpose must use AGENTS.md's **Tests that start
+red use the known-fail marker**, not plain `#[ignore]`. Keep the open issue,
+full test name, target and expected panic prefix accurate. A temporary red
+run for a fix does not justify shipping an unmarked failing test.
+
+## 3. Fix, then repeat the same measurement
+
+1. Continue `work-issue` only after the baseline demonstrates the defect.
+   Preserve the input and assertion. Do not weaken the expected result to
+   make the test pass, suppress a diagnostic, or remove a safety refusal.
+2. Make the smallest fix. Run the same MCP sequence or named test again.
+   Record the after reading and exact fixed head. For an MCP reproduction,
+   add a pinning test where possible; state any remaining coverage limit.
+3. Confirm that the test detects the defect: its recorded baseline run
+   must fail at the relevant assertion and its fixed run must pass.
+   If the assertion changed, repeat the baseline check in an isolated
+   worktree. Do not overwrite unrelated work to manufacture a red run.
+4. Run the selected quick gate and the other applicable checks from `gate`.
+   A dry run or zero-step plan is not a test pass. Keep full heavy lanes,
+   snapshots and release gates in their required lanes. Report unrelated
+   failures separately; do not replace actual output with expected output.
+
+## 4. Put the before reading in the PR
+
+Use this structure with actual readings, not placeholder success text:
+
+```text
+Reproduction before fix:
+- Baseline: <canonical main full SHA; build/binary provenance>
+- Input and environment: <fixture path and relevant settings>
+- Command or MCP requests: <repeatable sequence>
+- Expected: <assertion, diagnostic or numeric result>
+- Observed before: <actual result; log or evidence link>
+- Pinning test: <full name and baseline assertion failure, or limitation>
+
+After fix:
+- Head: <full fixed SHA>
+- Same measurement: <actual result; evidence link>
+- Checks: <commands and actual results>
+- Not exercised: <limits, unsupported routes or unrelated failures>
+```
+
+For prose-only work, replace the runtime fields with the before text,
+location and focused checks. Keep the normal PR fields from `work-issue`,
+including `Process change: yes` when applicable. Publish as a draft first.
+Verify publication and release writer ownership before independent review.
+A contributor pre-check is not a counted collaborator review.

+---
+name: takeover
+description: Continue another author's stalled CamCraft PR only with recorded approval or a stale claim. Check claims, branch ownership, maintainer edits, refresh timing and exact heads; preserve commits and provide a patch if a push is refused.
+---
+
+# takeover - continue a PR without competing with its author
+
+Use this skill for one named PR, not a sweep of old PRs. Read
+[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), [gh-issues](../gh-issues/SKILL.md),
+[issue-claims](../issue-claims/SKILL.md) and the
+[ownership guard](../issue-claims/references/ownership.md) first.
+AGENTS.md takes precedence. This procedure grants no repository permissions.
+
+## 1. Establish whether a takeover is allowed
+
+1. Read the complete issue and PR threads, reviews, labels and commits.
+   Search for other PRs with the same head repository and branch.
+   Record the issue, PR, head repository, branch, base and full exact SHAs.
+2. Stop during a release cut (an open `release/*` PR). Do not take a `P?`,
+   `blocked` or `needs-research` issue for implementation.
+3. Require the author's explicit approval in the thread, or evidence that
+   the claim is stale under **A claim must be live**. Link that evidence.
+   The age of the PR, silence on the PR, or a missing label is not enough.
+4. A contributor's claim remains live if any of these is true:
+   - The claimant has an open PR for the issue, even an old draft.
+   - The claimant's branch has a commit in the last 48 hours.
+   - The claimant commented on the issue in the last 48 hours.
+   Only when all three are absent can it be stale. Owner-account agent
+   claims use the separate 4-hour rule in `issue-claims`.
+5. Do not push while the author is active. Approval alone does not release
+   an active writer or reviewer. Obtain an explicit handoff and release.
+   A released writer record does not release a live issue claim. If the
+   claimant changes, record the old claim's withdrawal or release, then a
+   new claim. An ended claim never revives without a new claim line.
+6. Follow the ownership guard before dispatch or local work. A live writer
+   or counted reviewer means stand down and name the owner and record URL.
+   A counted reviewer has no expiry timer. Two active records mean STOP
+   until one owner releases. Failed or incomplete reads also mean STOP.
+
+## 2. Record one writer and prepare the existing branch
+
+1. Use `work-issue`'s existing-PR path. Keep the issue and its branch;
+   do not create a competing fix or overwrite the author's history.
+   Post or confirm one writer record on the upstream issue, and link it
+   from the PR. Include the approval or stale-claim evidence.
+2. Read the record back by its comment URL. Re-read the complete threads
+   and the exact remote head. Confirm the sole named writer before edits.
+3. Fetch the author's exact head into a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`.
+   Check that it equals the recorded `Starting head` and `Expected remote`.
+   Preserve the author's commits. Never rebase or force-push, including
+   `--force-with-lease`. Do not switch or edit the main checkout.
+4. Check GitHub's `maintainer_can_modify` field for the PR. Maintainer edits
+   let a base-repository maintainer update a permitted fork branch; the
+   flag does not give an arbitrary contributor push access. Confirm the
+   actual account, head repository and exact branch. Never infer access
+   from the flag alone. Do not use the author's credentials.
+5. Preserve the draft rules. New PRs open as drafts. An orange `conflicts`
+   verdict requires the `resolve-conflicts` draft-before-push procedure,
+   including its SAME exception. Ordinary review fixes keep a ready PR
+   ready under **A review finding does not make a PR a draft again**.
+   A takeover does not authorize an extra draft/ready cycle.
+
+## 3. Make and check the bounded change
+
+- Use [work-issue](../work-issue/SKILL.md) for the fix and its pinning tests.
+  For a bug, load [repro-first](../repro-first/SKILL.md) before the fix.
+- A takeover is not permission to refresh a branch. **Refresh only at merge
+  time** still applies: the author's agents handle **Own blocked PRs
+  first**, the PR is next in the merge batch, or the author chooses a
+  refresh while pushing a review fix. Otherwise leave the base alone.
+- For an allowed refresh, use
+  [resolve-conflicts](../resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md). Merge, never rebase.
+  Stop if both sides change the same logic or a safety rule can be lost.
+  Compile affected code with `cargo check --tests -p <affected-package>`,
+  one package at a time, including incoming base changes and shared inputs.
+  A prose-only refresh gets focused documentation checks, not a code pass.
+- Run the applicable checks on the final committed tree. Record the exact
+  head, commands, results and exclusions. A zero-step quick plan is not
+  proof that documentation or code passed tests.
+
+## 4. Publish once, or provide the patch
+
+1. Immediately before a push, repeat the ownership guard's pre-push reads.
+   Re-read the claims, writer/reviewer records, PR head and remote branch.
+   Do not build or edit between those reads and the push. A moved head
+   means STOP; preserve the local commits and report both exact SHAs.
+2. With confirmed maintainer-edit permission and a completed handoff, push
+   plainly to the recorded author's branch, not to upstream `main`.
+   A rejected push means STOP. Do not retry with another credential,
+   rebase, reset, branch deletion or force-push.
+3. If GitHub refuses the push, preserve the worktree and local commits.
+   Make a repository-relevant patch with
+   `git format-patch --stdout <starting-head>..HEAD`.
+   Post it in a PR comment as a fenced patch, or attach the patch and link
+   it from that comment if it exceeds the comment limit. Check that it
+   contains only the intended commits and no private data. Do not silently
+   open a replacement PR or push to a different branch.
+4. Write one result comment that names the starting head, each added
+   commit, the reason for each change, checks and any refusal. For a patch,
+   include its application base and state that the remote did not change.
+   For a successful push, verify remote and PR heads against local HEAD;
+   record `Published head` and `Expected remote` against the writer URL.
+5. Release writer ownership with its record URL, final exact head and the
+   published result or stopped reason. Read back the comment and patch.
+   Keep the issue open until its fix merges. Hand off for independent
+   review; never count your own pre-check as a collaborator review.
+
+## Completion check
+
+- Approval or all required stale-claim evidence is linked.
+- The author is not writing; the old claim and owners have valid releases.
+- One writer, the exact remote head and refresh permission were checked.
+- Original commits remain; no force-push or competing branch was used.
+- The result comment traces commits, reasons, checks and any refused push.
+- Remote publication or the patch was read back; ownership was released.

+//! The "not usable" refusal by name (#3545): when an operation's
+//! parameters fail `OpParams::is_sane`, the commands say which field
+//! broke which rule, in the field names that MCP and the project file
+//! use, so a caller can correct the call.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own domain model.
+
+use crate::operation::OpParams;
+use crate::project;
+
+/// Top-level fields that every kind carrying them asks to be positive
+/// (`OpParams::is_sane` and the nested kinds' own doors).
+const POSITIVE: [&str; 6] = [
+    "stepdown",
+    "stepover",
+    "feed",
+    "plunge_feed",
+    "tolerance",
+    "helix_radius",
+];
+
+/// Top-level fields that every kind carrying them asks to be 0 or more.
+const NON_NEGATIVE: [&str; 1] = ["stock_to_leave"];
+
+/// The refusal for parameters that failed `is_sane`: the generic
+/// sentence, followed by the first field that breaks its rule when
+/// one of the shared fields is the cause.
+pub(super) fn unusable(params: &OpParams) -> String {
+    let head = format!(
+        "operation parameters are not usable for a {} operation",
+        params.kind()
+    );
+    match field_problem(params) {
+        Some(why) => format!("{head}: {why}"),
+        None => head,
+    }
+}
+
+/// The first shared field that breaks its rule, by name and value.
+/// Nested objects (a wire's 4-axis block, a tilt) are not read: their
+/// fields have rules of their own.
+fn field_problem(params: &OpParams) -> Option<String> {
+    let json = project::params_to_json(params);
+    // The parameters are externally tagged: `{ "<kind>": { fields } }`.
+    let fields = json.as_object()?.values().next()?.as_object()?;
+    let number = |key: &str| fields.get(key).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_f64);
+    POSITIVE
+        .iter()
+        .find_map(|&key| {
+            number(key)
+                .filter(|v| !(v.is_finite() && *v > 0.0))
+                .map(|v| format!("{key} must be greater than 0 (got {v})"))
+        })
+        .or_else(|| {
+            NON_NEGATIVE.iter().find_map(|&key| {
+                number(key)
+                    .filter(|v| !(v.is_finite() && *v >= 0.0))
+                    .map(|v| format!("{key} must be 0 or more (got {v})"))
+            })
+        })
+}

+//! Hidden alias names of renamed built-in posts (#3537, #4000). Provenance:
+//! CamCraft's own post registry history; no list shows an alias name.
+//!
+//! A saved project (document post, setup post, option key `builtin:<name>`),
+//! a script `cps:`, an MCP or CLI post name and a machine `controller.post`
+//! that still say an old name select the registry name. A save writes the
+//! registry name.
+
+use crate::schema::PostRef;
+
+/// `(old name, registry name)`, one row for each old name of a built-in post.
+pub const POST_ALIASES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
+    // #3537 renamed it; #4000 renamed it again.
+    ("Agie native wire EDM", super::agie::POST),
+    // #4000: the name between #3537 and #4000.
+    ("Native wire EDM job files", super::agie::POST),
+];
+
+/// The registry name that `name` selects: the registry name for an alias, else `name`.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_name(name: &str) -> &str {
+    POST_ALIASES
+        .iter()
+        .find(|(old, _)| *old == name)
+        .map_or(name, |(_, new)| *new)
+}
+
+/// `post` with an alias name replaced by the registry name it selects.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_ref(post: PostRef) -> PostRef {
+    match post {
+        PostRef::Named(name) => PostRef::Named(current_name(&name).to_owned()),
+        other => other,
+    }
+}
+
+/// An option key `builtin:<alias>` rewritten to the key of the registry name.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_key(key: &str) -> String {
+    match key.strip_prefix("builtin:") {
+        Some(name) => format!("builtin:{}", current_name(name)),
+        None => key.to_owned(),
+    }
+}

+//! A selected reentrant DXF die opening of lines and arcs through the public CLI and the
+//! native post (#3178). Provenance: the original examples/agie/reentrant-die drawing and
+//! the control-checked DIE20 setup of #2957.
+use super::dxf::run;
+use std::fs;
+
+const SCRIPT: &str = include_str!("../../../../examples/agie/reentrant-die.camscript");
+const DXF: &str = include_str!("../../../../examples/agie/reentrant-die.dxf");
+const DIE20: &str = include_str!("../../../post/tests/golden/agie-setup/DIE20.SBL");
+
+fn script() -> String {
+    SCRIPT.replace("reentrant-die", "racetrack")
+}
+
+/// The control-checked die setup with only the stem, the 80 x 60 stock and the hole changed.
+fn die_setup(stem: &str, hole: [&str; 2]) -> String {
+    let piece = |field: &str, value: &str| format!("NULL,{field},"{value}",je_dim)");
+    let hole_at = |axis: &str, value: &str| format!(""stp1",ID_POS{axis},"{value}",je_dim)");
+    DIE20
+        .replace(&piece("ID_DIML", "70.000"), &piece("ID_DIML", "80.000"))
+        .replace(&piece("ID_DIMB", "70.000"), &piece("ID_DIMB", "60.000"))
+        .replace(&piece("ID_POSPOSX", "-35.000"), &piece("ID_POSPOSX", "-40.000"))
+        .replace(&piece("ID_POSPOSY", "-35.000"), &piece("ID_POSPOSY", "-30.000"))
+        .replace(&hole_at("X", "-5.500"), &hole_at("X", hole[0]))
+        .replace(&hole_at("Y", "0.000"), &hole_at("Y", hole[1]))
+        .replace("DIE20", stem)
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_reentrant_line_and_arc_die_posts_g02_g03_and_the_checked_die_setup() {
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let output = run(dir.path(), &script(), DXF);
+    assert!(output.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));
+    let job = dir.path().join("REENT20");
+    // The golden is explained line by line in camcraft_post's opening_tests.
+    assert_eq!(
+        fs::read(job.join("REENT20.ISO")).unwrap(),
+        include_bytes!("../golden/nc/agie-native/REENT20.ISO").as_slice()
+    );
+    let sbl = fs::read_to_string(job.join("REENT20.SBL")).unwrap();
+    assert_ne!(die_setup("REENT20", ["0.000", "-7.000"]), DIE20.replace("DIE20", "REENT20"));
+    assert_eq!(sbl, die_setup("REENT20", ["0.000", "-7.000"]));
+    assert!(sbl.contains("ID_PUNCH,c_die"));
+    assert_eq!(
+        fs::read_to_string(job.join("REENT20.SBR")).unwrap(),
+        "AGIE.USING_REENT20.ISO IMPORT REENT20.ISO;
"
+    );
+}
+

+        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

+fn refused(text: &str, start: &str, words: &str) {

+fn cyclic_missing_and_too_deep_blocks_are_refused_by_name() {
+    refused(&drawing(&block("A", &insert("A", "")), &insert("A", "")), "INSERT A", "cyclic block reference");
+    let pair = format!("{}{}", block("A", &insert("b", "")), block("B", &insert("a", "")));
+    refused(&drawing(&pair, &insert("A", "")), "INSERT a", "cyclic block reference");
+    refused(&drawing(&block("A", LINE), &insert("Nope", "")), "INSERT Nope", "block is not defined");
+    refused(&drawing(&block("A", &insert("Gone", "")), &insert("A", "")), "INSERT Gone", "block is not defined");
+    // A chain of `levels` nested blocks: L1 inserts L2, ... the last holds a line.
+    let chain = |levels: usize| {
+        let mut blocks: String = (1..levels).map(|i| block(&format!("L{i}"), &insert(&format!("L{}", i + 1), ""))).collect();

+    let doc = parse(chain(MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH).as_bytes()).expect("nesting at the bound reads");
+    assert_eq!(doc.primitives.len(), 1);
+    refused(&chain(MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH + 1), "INSERT L9", "blocks nest deeper than 8 levels");

+//! The HEIDENHAIN profile table (#4095): control model, NC software family
+//! and release range to the flag values of the profile.
+//!
+//! Provenance: `docs/research/heidenhain/dialects.md` section 3 (profiles)
+//! and `differences.md` sections B, B2 and B3 (HEIDENHAIN manual IDs and
+//! pages). Each flag and its source is listed in
+//! `docs/decisions/4095-heidenhain-dialect-resolver.md`. Release lists name
+//! only the releases that the research names (as #4172 did): an unnamed
+//! release is refused, never assumed.
+
+use serde::Serialize;
+
+/// A fact that the research settles (`Yes`/`No`) or does not (`Unknown`).
+/// A post refuses a function whose flag is `Unknown`.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub enum Tri {
+    Yes,
+    No,
+    Unknown,
+}
+
+/// The cycle 200 (DRILLING) parameter level (`differences.md` B2, "Cycle
+/// 200 Q list"). Each level includes the one before.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub enum C200 {
+    /// Q200 Q201 Q206 Q202 Q210 Q203 Q204.
+    Base,
+    /// + Q211 (dwell time at the depth).
+    Q211,
+    /// + Q395 (depth reference).
+    Q395,
+}
+
+/// What cycle 247 (DATUM SETTING) does (`differences.md` B2, "Cycle 247").
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub enum Cycle247 {
+    /// The control has no cycle 247.
+    None,
+    /// It sets a datum value (before iTNC 530 340 422).
+    Datum,
+    /// It activates a row of the preset table.
+    PresetTable,
+    Unknown,
+}
+
+/// The Klartext dwell form (`differences.md` B2, "Cycle 9" and
+/// "FUNCTION DWELL"). DIN/ISO always writes `G04 F` (cycle 9).
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub enum Dwell {
+    Cycle9,
+    FunctionDwell,
+    Unknown,
+}
+
+/// The capability flags of one profile.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub struct Flags {
+    /// DIN/ISO programs exist on this control and version.
+    pub language_iso: Tri,
+    /// Coordinate decimals: 3 (1 µm input) or 4 (0.1 µm input).
+    pub decimals: u8,
+    /// `TOOL CALL "NAME"` is permitted.
+    pub tool_call_by_name: Tri,
+    /// The tool name length in TOOL CALL / TOOL DEF (0 without names).
+    pub tool_name_max: u8,
+    /// `L M140 MB MAX` (retract along the tool axis).
+    pub m140: Tri,
+    /// M136/M137 (feed per revolution / per minute).
+    #[serde(rename = "m136m137")]
+    pub m136_m137: Tri,
+    /// The cycle 200 (DRILLING) parameter level.
+    pub drill_c200: C200,
+    /// The meaning of cycle 247 (DATUM SETTING).
+    pub cycle247: Cycle247,
+    /// The Klartext dwell form.
+    pub dwell: Dwell,
+}
+
+/// The NC software identifiers of one row.
+pub(super) enum Ids {
+    /// Named 6-digit identifiers (the old controls, iTNC 530 340 420/422).
+    Exact(&'static [u32]),
+    /// A 5-digit family and a variant range (the sixth digit).
+    Family { fam: u32, vmin: u32, vmax: u32 },
+}
+
+/// The releases of one row.
+pub(super) enum Rels {
+    /// The research names no release: each release `01`..`99`.
+    Any,
+    Range(u8, u8),
+    List(&'static [u8]),
+}
+
+pub(super) struct Row {
+    pub profile: &'static str,
+    pub models: &'static [&'static str],
+    pub ids: Ids,
+    pub rels: Rels,
+    pub flags: Flags,
+}
+
+/// TNC 124 and TNC 128: one axis in each block, no arcs (`differences.md` A.1).
+pub(super) const PARAXIAL: &[&str] = &["TNC 124", "TNC 128"];
+
+use C200::{Base, Q211, Q395};
+use Tri::{No, Unknown, Yes};
+
+const TNC310: Flags = Flags {
+    language_iso: No,

+    tool_call_by_name: No,
+    tool_name_max: 0,
+    m140: No,
+    m136_m137: Unknown,
+    drill_c200: Base,
+    cycle247: Cycle247::None,
+    dwell: Dwell::Unknown,
+};
+const TNC410: Flags = Flags { language_iso: Yes, m136_m137: No, dwell: Dwell::Cycle9, ..TNC310 };
+const TNC426A: Flags = Flags {

+const TNC426_474: Flags = Flags { drill_c200: Q211, ..TNC426_472 };
+const TNC426_476: Flags = Flags { m140: Yes, cycle247: Cycle247::Datum, ..TNC426_474 };
+const ITNC_420: Flags = Flags {

+    cycle247: Cycle247::Datum,
+    dwell: Dwell::Cycle9,

+const ITNC_422: Flags = Flags { cycle247: Cycle247::PresetTable, ..ITNC_420 };
+const ITNC_604: Flags = Flags { drill_c200: Q395, ..ITNC_422 };
+const TNC320_EARLY: Flags = Flags {
+    language_iso: Unknown,
+    decimals: 4,
+    tool_call_by_name: Yes,
+    tool_name_max: 16,
+    m140: Yes,
+    m136_m137: Unknown,
+    drill_c200: Q211,
+    cycle247: Cycle247::Unknown,
+    dwell: Dwell::Cycle9,
+};

+//! The 50-size steep-taper holders of the built-in holder library
+//! (#3919): BT50 (JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 BT) and CAT50 (ASME B5.50), in
+//! ER collet chuck and Weldon side-lock versions. Specced from the
+//! taper tables as tooling makers publish them (the numbers and their
+//! sources are in docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders-2.md); the
+//! outlines are our own conservative bodies, drawn by the laws of
+//! `holder_library.rs` (full flange cylinder, 45-degree flare, the
+//! profile stops at the gauge line), not any vendor's model.
+
+use super::{family, HolderEntry, Taper, ER16, ER20, ER25, ER32, ER40, ER50, INCH_BORES, METRIC_BORES};
+
+/// JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 BT50: Ø69.85 gauge, Ø100 flange, 3 from the
+/// gauge line to the flange's back face, a 35 thick flange (its front
+/// face 38 from the gauge line).
+pub const BT50: Taper = Taper { name: "BT50", ring: "flange", gauge_d: 69.85, flange_d: 100.0, standoff: 3.0, flange_t: 35.0 };
+/// ASME B5.50 size 50 (CAT50, V-flange): 2.750 in gauge, 3.875 in
+/// flange, 0.125 in standoff, 0.625 in flange (front face 0.750 in from
+/// the gauge line) - the CAT40 standoff and flange on the 50 taper.
+pub const CAT50: Taper = Taper { name: "CAT50", ring: "flange", gauge_d: 69.85, flange_d: 98.425, standoff: 3.175, flange_t: 15.875 };
+
+/// The default gauge length (mm, gauge line to nose face) of every
+/// 50-taper entry: a typical catalog length for the size.
+const GAUGE: f64 = 100.0;
+
+/// The BT50 and CAT50 entries, in the editor's order: each taper's ER
+/// chucks (ER16-ER50, the whole ER table but ER11), then every Weldon
+/// bore - a 50-taper body carries the largest of them.
+pub(super) fn entries() -> Vec<HolderEntry> {
+    let ers = [(ER16, GAUGE), (ER20, GAUGE), (ER25, GAUGE), (ER32, GAUGE), (ER40, GAUGE), (ER50, GAUGE)];
+    let mut v = family(BT50, &ers, METRIC_BORES.iter().chain(INCH_BORES.iter()), GAUGE);
+    v.extend(family(CAT50, &ers, INCH_BORES.iter().chain(METRIC_BORES.iter()), GAUGE));
+    v
+}

+//! #3642: the letter codes an indexable insert designation is built
+//! from - shape, clearance, tolerance class and fixing - as typed
+//! values with their letters. Our own tables of the code meanings that
+//! the ISO 1832 designation system publishes and that tool vendors
+//! print in their catalogs; no standard text is copied.
+
+/// Position 1: the insert's shape, read by its corner angle.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum InsertShape {
+    /// Parallelogram, 85 degrees.
+    A,
+    /// Parallelogram, 82 degrees.
+    B,
+    /// Rhombic, 80 degrees.
+    C,
+    /// Rhombic, 55 degrees.
+    D,
+    /// Rhombic, 75 degrees.
+    E,
+    /// Hexagon, 120 degrees.
+    H,
+    /// Parallelogram, 55 degrees.
+    K,
+    /// Rectangle, 90 degrees.
+    L,
+    /// Rhombic, 86 degrees.
+    M,
+    /// Octagon, 135 degrees.
+    O,
+    /// Pentagon, 108 degrees.
+    P,
+    /// Round.
+    R,
+    /// Square, 90 degrees.
+    S,
+    /// Triangle, 60 degrees.
+    T,
+    /// Rhombic, 35 degrees.
+    V,
+    /// Trigon, 80 degrees.
+    W,
+}
+
+/// The shape letters in one place, for the parsers' refusals.
+pub const SHAPE_LETTERS: &str = "A B C D E H K L M O P R S T V W";
+
+impl InsertShape {
+    /// The shape for its letter; `None` for a letter that is not one.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_letter(c: char) -> Option<Self> {
+        Some(match c {
+            'A' => Self::A,
+            'B' => Self::B,
+            'C' => Self::C,
+            'D' => Self::D,
+            'E' => Self::E,
+            'H' => Self::H,
+            'K' => Self::K,
+            'L' => Self::L,
+            'M' => Self::M,
+            'O' => Self::O,
+            'P' => Self::P,
+            'R' => Self::R,
+            'S' => Self::S,
+            'T' => Self::T,
+            'V' => Self::V,
+            'W' => Self::W,
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn letter(self) -> char {
+        match self {
+            Self::A => 'A',
+            Self::B => 'B',
+            Self::C => 'C',
+            Self::D => 'D',
+            Self::E => 'E',
+            Self::H => 'H',
+            Self::K => 'K',
+            Self::L => 'L',
+            Self::M => 'M',
+            Self::O => 'O',
+            Self::P => 'P',
+            Self::R => 'R',
+            Self::S => 'S',
+            Self::T => 'T',
+            Self::V => 'V',
+            Self::W => 'W',
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The corner angle in degrees; `None` for a round insert.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn corner_deg(self) -> Option<f64> {
+        Some(match self {
+            Self::A => 85.0,
+            Self::B => 82.0,
+            Self::C | Self::W => 80.0,
+            Self::D | Self::K => 55.0,
+            Self::E => 75.0,
+            Self::H => 120.0,
+            Self::L | Self::S => 90.0,
+            Self::M => 86.0,
+            Self::O => 135.0,
+            Self::P => 108.0,
+            Self::T => 60.0,
+            Self::V => 35.0,
+            Self::R => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// The edge length over the inscribed circle's diameter, for the
+    /// shapes whose every edge touches that circle. Each edge is the
+    /// two tangent lengths from its end corners, `r / tan(a / 2)`. A
+    /// trigon alternates 80 and 160 degree corners. `None` for a
+    /// parallelogram or a rectangle (no circle touches all four
+    /// edges) and for a round insert (its size is its diameter).
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn edge_per_ic(self) -> Option<f64> {
+        let cot_half = |deg: f64| 1.0 / (deg.to_radians() * 0.5).tan();
+        // The edge in units of the radius, halved to units of the diameter.
+        let per_r = match self {
+            Self::C | Self::D | Self::E | Self::M | Self::V => {
+                let a = self.corner_deg()?;
+                cot_half(a) + cot_half(180.0 - a)
+            }
+            Self::S | Self::T | Self::H | Self::O | Self::P => 2.0 * cot_half(self.corner_deg()?),
+            Self::W => cot_half(80.0) + cot_half(160.0),
+            Self::A | Self::B | Self::K | Self::L | Self::R => return None,
+        };
+        Some(per_r * 0.5)
+    }
+}

+    }
+}

+/// Position 3: the tolerance class letters. Kept as its letter: no

+
+/// Position 4: how the insert is held and whether it has a chip

+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]

+    /// No hole, chip breaker on one face.
+    R,
+    /// No hole, chip breakers on both faces.
+    F,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, no chip breaker.
+    A,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, chip breaker on one face.
+    M,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, chip breakers on both faces.
+    G,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (40-60 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    W,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (40-60 degrees), chip breaker.
+    T,
+    /// Hole countersunk on both faces (40-60 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    Q,

+//! #3643: why a lathe tool assembly is refused. Each refusal names the
+//! component, or the value, that it is about. Our own wording.
+
+use crate::lathe_holder::LatheBodyError;
+use crate::tool_assembly::AssemblyError;
+
+/// Why a lathe assembly is refused.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub enum LatheAssemblyError {
+    /// A refusal of the component chain (fits, frames, ports, cycles).
+    Assembly(AssemblyError),
+    NotInsert {
+        name: String,
+    },
+    NoSeat {
+        name: String,
+    },
+    NoNose {
+        name: String,
+        code: String,
+    },
+    Orientation {
+        q: u8,
+    },
+    NeedOrientation {
+        name: String,
+        coupling: String,
+    },
+    Station(LatheBodyError),
+    SpunBody {
+        name: String,
+    },
+    /// A body point stands `reach` mm along the cutting direction on
+    /// `axis`, past the insert's cutting line at `nose` mm.
+    BodyPastEdge {
+        name: String,
+        axis: char,
+        reach: f64,
+        nose: f64,
+    },
+    Clearance(LatheBodyError),
+}
+
+impl core::fmt::Display for LatheAssemblyError {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
+        match self {
+            Self::Assembly(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
+            Self::NotInsert { name } => {
+                write!(f, "the cutting item '{name}' is not an insert - a lathe assembly cuts with an insert in a seat")
+            }
+            Self::NoSeat { name } => write!(f, "the insert '{name}' does not sit in an insert seat"),
+            Self::NoNose { name, code } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the insert '{name}' ({code}) states no nose radius - a turning insert needs a corner radius more than 0 mm"
+            ),
+            Self::Orientation { q } => write!(f, "the lathe orientation {q} is not valid - it takes 1 to 8"),
+            Self::NeedOrientation { name, coupling } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the orientation of '{name}' cannot be derived from its coupling {coupling} - state the orientation (1 to 8)"
+            ),
+            Self::Station(e) => write!(f, "the lathe station is refused: {e}"),
+            Self::SpunBody { name } => write!(
+                f,
+                "'{name}' has a revolved body - a lathe component's body is a box or a mesh, because it does not turn"
+            ),
+            Self::BodyPastEdge { name, axis, reach, nose } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the body of '{name}' reaches {reach:.3} mm from the nose centre along the cutting direction in {axis}, \
+                 past the insert's cutting line at {nose:.3} mm - check the hand, the orientation or the seat frame"
+            ),
+            Self::Clearance(e) => write!(f, "the lathe assembly's body is refused: {e}"),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl std::error::Error for LatheAssemblyError {}
+
+impl From<AssemblyError> for LatheAssemblyError {
+    fn from(e: AssemblyError) -> Self {
+        Self::Assembly(e)
+    }
+}

+use crate::tool_assembly::AssemblyError;
+
+/// Why a multi-seat milling cutter is refused.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub enum MillingError {
+    /// A stated number is NaN or infinite.
+    NonFinite { name: String, what: &'static str, value: f64 },
+    /// The cutting diameter `DC` is not over 0, or past the tool cap.
+    BadDiameter { name: String, dc: f64 },
+    /// The cutting edge angle is not over 0 and at most 90 degrees.
+    BadLeadAngle { name: String, deg: f64 },
+    /// The largest axial depth `APMX` is not over 0.
+    BadDepth { name: String, apmx: f64 },
+    /// The component is not a tool item (a cutter body with seats).
+    NotABody { name: String },
+    /// A stated seat count of 0.
+    NoSeats { name: String },
+    /// More seats than a tool record counts flutes.
+    TooManySeats { name: String, count: usize },
+    /// A stated seat count that the body's seat ports contradict.
+    SeatCount { name: String, stated: u32, ports: usize },
+    /// A seat that does not take the shared insert (#3642's check).
+    Fit(FitError),
+    /// The insert's corner does not fit the cutter.
+    Corner { name: String, why: String },
+    /// The tool record that the cutter gives fails the tool law.
+    Tool { name: String, why: String },
+    /// The seat geometry of the assembly puts the cutting point on a
+    /// diameter other than the stated `DC`.
+    SeatDiameter { name: String, seat_d: f64, dc: f64 },
+    /// A judged body stands outside the cutter inside the cutting depth:
+    /// `cut_r` is how far the tool reaches at the band's lowest point.
+    BodyOutside { name: String, above: f64, r: f64, cut_r: f64 },
+    /// The spindle assembly is refused by the resolver (#3643); boxed,
+    /// so that every result of this module stays small.
+    Assembly { name: String, err: Box<AssemblyError> },
+    /// The assembly mounts a cutter body or an insert other than the
+    /// ones the cutter was derived from.
+    Mismatch { name: String, why: String },
+    /// A seat of the assembly is not the mounted seat turned about the
+    /// spindle axis: `what` is "frame", "radius", "height" or
+    /// "orientation".
+    SeatOff { name: String, port: String, what: &'static str, why: String },
+}
+
+impl core::fmt::Display for MillingError {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
+        match self {
+            Self::NonFinite { name, what, value } => write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' has a non-finite {what} ({value})"),
+            Self::BadDiameter { name, dc } => {
+                write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' has a cutting diameter of {dc} mm - it must be over 0 and at most 500 mm")
+            }
+            Self::BadLeadAngle { name, deg } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the cutter '{name}' has a cutting edge angle of {deg} degrees - it must be over 0 and at most 90"
+            ),
+            Self::BadDepth { name, apmx } => {
+                write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' has a largest cutting depth of {apmx} mm - it must be over 0")
+            }
+            Self::NotABody { name } => {
+                write!(f, "'{name}' is not a cutter body - a multi-seat cutter needs a tool item with insert seats")
+            }
+            Self::NoSeats { name } => write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' states 0 seats - it needs one at least"),
+            Self::TooManySeats { name, count } => {
+                write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' has {count} seats - a tool counts 32 cutting edges at most")
+            }
+            Self::SeatCount { name, stated, ports } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the cutter '{name}' states {stated} seats, but its body has {ports} seat ports - state one seat port for a seat count, or a port for each seat"
+            ),
+            Self::Fit(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
+            Self::Corner { name, why } => write!(f, "the insert corner of the cutter '{name}' is refused: {why}"),
+            Self::Tool { name, why } => write!(f, "the cutter '{name}' gives a tool that is refused: {why}"),
+            Self::SeatDiameter { name, seat_d, dc } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the seats of the cutter '{name}' put the cutting point on Ø{seat_d:.3} mm, but the cutter states DC {dc} mm"
+            ),
+            Self::BodyOutside { name, above, r, cut_r } => write!(
+                f,
+                "a body of the cutter '{name}' reaches {r:.3} mm from the axis at {above:.3} mm above the tip - outside the {cut_r:.3} mm that the tool reaches there, inside the cutting depth"
+            ),
+            Self::Assembly { name, err } => write!(f, "the assembly of the cutter '{name}' is refused: {err}"),
+            Self::Mismatch { name, why } => write!(f, "the assembly does not match the cutter '{name}': {why}"),
+            Self::SeatOff { name, port, why, .. } => {
+                write!(f, "the seat {port} of the cutter '{name}' is refused: {why}")
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl std::error::Error for MillingError {}
+
+impl From<FitError> for MillingError {
+    fn from(e: FitError) -> Self {
+        Self::Fit(e)
+    }
+}

+//! #3643: why a tool assembly is refused. Each refusal names the
+//! component (and the port) it is about. Our own wording.
+
+use crate::component_fit::FitError;
+use crate::frame::FrameError;
+use crate::spun::SpunError;
+
+/// Why an assembly is refused.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub enum AssemblyError {
+    Empty,
+    TooMany { count: usize },
+    NoRoot,
+    TwoRoots { a: String, b: String },
+    InsertAtRoot { name: String },
+    BadParent { name: String, parent: usize },
+    Cycle { name: String },
+    NoPort { parent: String },
+    AmbiguousPort { parent: String, ports: String },
+    PortTaken { parent: String, port: String },
+    Fit(FitError),
+    NoCutter,
+    TwoCutters { a: String, b: String },
+    MissingFrame { name: String, port: String },
+    NonFinite { name: String, what: &'static str },
+    BadFrame { name: String, err: FrameError },
+    Stickout { name: String, why: &'static str },
+    OffAxis { name: String },
+    BadGauge { gauge_len: f64 },
+    BadCutter { name: String, why: String },
+    Body { name: String, err: SpunError },
+    BodyInFlutes { bottom: f64, flute_len: f64 },
+}
+
+impl core::fmt::Display for AssemblyError {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
+        match self {
+            Self::Empty => write!(f, "the tool assembly has no components"),
+            Self::TooMany { count } => {
+                write!(f, "the tool assembly has {count} components - {} at most", super::MAX_NODES)
+            }
+            Self::NoRoot => write!(f, "no component of the tool assembly sits on the spindle (each one has a parent)"),
+            Self::TwoRoots { a, b } => write!(f, "'{a}' and '{b}' both sit on the spindle - an assembly has one root"),
+            Self::InsertAtRoot { name } => write!(f, "the insert '{name}' cannot sit on the spindle - it needs a seat"),
+            Self::BadParent { name, parent } => write!(f, "'{name}' names component {parent} as its parent, which is not in the assembly"),
+            Self::Cycle { name } => write!(f, "'{name}' is in a cycle of mounts - it never reaches the spindle"),
+            Self::NoPort { parent } => write!(f, "'{parent}' has no port for a component to sit on"),
+            Self::AmbiguousPort { parent, ports } => {
+                write!(f, "'{parent}' has the ports {ports} - name the port the component sits on")
+            }
+            Self::PortTaken { parent, port } => write!(f, "two components sit on the port {port} of '{parent}'"),
+            Self::Fit(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
+            Self::NoCutter => write!(f, "the tool assembly has no cutting item (an insert or a solid tool)"),
+            Self::TwoCutters { a, b } => {
+                write!(f, "'{a}' and '{b}' are both cutting items - a spindle assembly has one active cutting tip")
+            }
+            Self::MissingFrame { name, port } => write!(f, "'{name}' has no frame for its port {port}"),
+            Self::NonFinite { name, what } => write!(f, "'{name}' has a non-finite {what}"),
+            Self::BadFrame { name, err } => write!(f, "'{name}': {err}"),
+            Self::Stickout { name, why } => write!(f, "the stickout of '{name}' is refused: {why}"),
+            Self::OffAxis { name } => write!(f, "'{name}' does not stand on the spindle axis - a spindle body must be coaxial"),
+            Self::BadGauge { gauge_len } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the gauge length works out to {gauge_len} mm - the cutting tip must sit below the spindle face, within {} mm",
+                crate::holder_profile::MAX_BODY_HEIGHT
+            ),
+            Self::BadCutter { name, why } => write!(f, "the cutting item '{name}' is refused: {why}"),
+            Self::Body { name, err } => write!(f, "the body of '{name}' is refused: {err}"),
+            Self::BodyInFlutes { bottom, flute_len } => write!(
+                f,
+                "the assembled body reaches into the flutes (its foot is {bottom:.3} mm above the tip, the flutes run {flute_len:.3} mm)"
+            ),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl std::error::Error for AssemblyError {}

+# Recorded AI replay fixtures (format 1)
+
+These files replay **recorded model output**, not successful machining recipes.
+The tests use the real AI panel, worker, argument parser, MCP inbox, document,
+and undo history. Only `ChatTransport::complete` is replaced. No network or
+model installation is needed.
+
+## Source and correspondence
+
+Source: [mkinney/Camcraft, q08 QA recording](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/tree/d9be74b1408654799446f0e05e2c675fefc619c2/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z).
+The source commit is `d9be74b1408654799446f0e05e2c675fefc619c2`.
+The transcript blob is `09832301703903e2bc3ced24bd7bc785f4dce4ff`.
+Its SHA-256 is `1746eb81dfd556db0c29183a4effc58d16b35db29efd1e8bda6485abd2b9a275`.
+
+The model was `qwen3-coder:latest` on local Ollama. The recorded application
+was CamCraft v0.25.0 (`7e2a8119`), Linux x86_64, Native tools mode, with the
+`Offline local (Ollama)` preset. The original `meta` object is retained.
+The recorder captured the requests and replies, not an application export.
+See [the recorder's explanation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3411#issuecomment-7079851491).
+
+| Fixture | Original zero-based turn | Initial state | Recorded outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `q08-finishing.json` | 1 (session 1, step 2) | Original `q08-start.camproj` | Adds `Pocket finishing`; three argument/source refusals; later edits leave 0.1 mm stock and `waterline`. |
+| `q08-edit.json` | 3 (session 1, step 4) | Start project plus the finishing operation from `job-03-after-step3.json` | Changes only the finishing operation. The model deletes and re-adds it, then leaves climb=true, stepdown=0.1, stock=0.05. |
+| `q08-delete.json` | 7 (session 2, step 6) | Original `q08-after-step5.camproj` | Two native delete calls. Current policy must wait for each Allow/Deny decision. |
+
+Each slice contains the **whole recorded turn**, including all 12 rounds
+when the original panel reached its round cap. No final reply is invented.
+The finishing and edit requests did **not** achieve their requested zero
+stock and 0.2 mm stepdown. The tests pin the actual document, not the model's
+claim of success. The roughing operation must retain all recorded parameters.
+This is not a new recording of a successful edit-only model workflow.
+
+For the edit slice, `setup` reconstructs the intermediate operation from the
+recorded job snapshot. Its `params.pocket` is flattened for `add_operation`,
+as that tool requires. This is explicit test setup, not a recorded reply.
+The start project supplies the original model, selection, stock and tool.
+The smaller catalog tool is added before the reconstructed operation.
+
+The source's historical delete calls ran without confirmation (#3424).
+The replay does **not** preserve that bug. Both denial and approval are
+tested against the current policy. A denial preserves the document and
+history, even though the recorded final text claims that all operations
+were deleted. Historical missing system prompts (#3425) are not recreated.
+
+## Format
+
+One JSON object describes one conversation slice:
+
+- `format_version`: currently `1`; unknown versions fail.
+- `source`: repository, immutable commit, transcript path, and zero-based
+  `turn_indices`. `setup_snapshot` names an intermediate job snapshot.
+- `meta`: the original recording metadata, unchanged.
+- `initial_project`: one of the checked-in recorded `.camproj` files.
+- `setup`: explicit MCP calls that reconstruct the slice's initial state.
+- `turns`: original `user`, `session`, `brief_step`, and ordered `rounds`.
+  Each round retains `model_reply` and `usage` from the recording.
+- `refused_call_ids`: argument/source refusals that must produce failed
+  cards, rendered explanations, and real error replies to the model.
+- `expected_operations`: the original job snapshot projected to operation
+  name, kind, tool, source and parameters, in document order.
+
+`ReplayTransport` wraps the captured message fields in the OpenAI-compatible
+`choices[0].message` envelope expected by the shipping parser. It retains
+`finish_reason`, call IDs, index, function names, raw argument **strings**,
+and content. It never extracts tool calls from plain text or normalizes
+argument JSON. Exhaustion and unconsumed replies fail the test.
+
+The original historical `tool_results_sent_this_round` are not replayed.
+The real current dispatcher produces those results. The original snapshots
+supply expected document values; they are not returned by a fake MCP server.
+New additive schema fields are permitted, but every recorded parameter and
+source field must match. Operation counts and order must match exactly.
+Transient toolpaths, collision results and status caches are not goldens.
+Undo and redo are checked against the real before/after document states.
+These software tests do not establish physical-machine safety.
+
+Both `.camproj` files are unchanged copies from the source directory.
+Their original source paths identify public QA assets; replay uses the
+embedded facets and does not read those external paths.
+
+To record another fixture, follow [the recording guide](../../../../../../../docs/agents/ai-chat-replay.md).

+//! The viewport overlay inks are theme tokens (#1120): each built-in
+//! column keeps the colour the draw site wrote as a literal before, so
+//! the move changes no pixel, and a theme file can set each ink by name.
+//! The view cube inks follow the viewport ground, as they did before.
+//! Provenance: our own tests over our own token table and theme format.
+//!
+//! A module of the `theme_files` suite (#3187: no new test binary).
+
+use camcraft_ui::egui_app::theme::Tokens;
+use camcraft_ui::egui_app::theme_files as tf;
+use egui::Color32;
+
+/// The handle and pick inks of a token table.
+fn inks(t: &Tokens) -> [Color32; 3] {
+    [t.handle_shade, t.handle_text, t.pick_rim]
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_built_in_columns_keep_the_handle_and_pick_colours() {
+    // The literals of `move_handles.rs`, `turn_handles.rs` and
+    // `align_pick_viz.rs` before #1120, in both columns: the handles and
+    // the picks draw over the 3D view, whose ink does not follow the
+    // chrome's column.
+    let before = [
+        Color32::from_black_alpha(170),
+        Color32::WHITE,
+        Color32::from_rgb(245, 240, 250),
+    ];
+    assert_eq!(inks(&Tokens::DARK), before, "dark column");
+    assert_eq!(inks(&Tokens::LIGHT), before, "light column");
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_theme_file_sets_each_handle_and_pick_ink_by_name() {
+    let text = r##"{
+        "format": "camcraft-theme/1",
+        "descriptor": { "name": "inks" },
+        "base": "dark",
+        "colors": { "handle_shade": "#10203040", "handle_text": "#FFEE00", "pick_rim": "#00FF88" }
+    }"##;
+    let theme =
+        tf::parse_text(text, "inks.json").unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("the theme reads: {e}"));
+    assert_eq!(
+        inks(&theme.tokens),
+        [
+            Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x40),
+            Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xEE, 0x00),
+            Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0xFF, 0x88),
+        ]
+    );
+    assert!(
+        theme.notes.is_empty(),
+        "each key is known: {:?}",
+        theme.notes
+    );
+    for name in ["handle_shade", "handle_text", "pick_rim"] {
+        assert!(
+            tf::COLOR_NAMES.contains(&name),
+            "{name} is a colour key of the theme format"
+        );
+    }
+}
+
+/// The view cube, marker, axis and hover inks of a token table.
+fn furniture(t: &Tokens) -> [Color32; 12] {
+    [
+        t.cube_edge,
+        t.cube_label,
+        t.cube_glyph_on,
+        t.cube_glyph_off,
+        t.viewport_hint,
+        t.marker_stem,
+        t.marker_ring,
+        t.marker_dot,
+        t.axis_x,
+        t.axis_y,
+        t.axis_z,
+        t.viewport_hover,
+    ]
+}
+
+const FURNITURE_KEYS: [&str; 12] = [
+    "cube_edge",
+    "cube_label",
+    "cube_glyph_on",
+    "cube_glyph_off",
+    "viewport_hint",
+    "marker_stem",
+    "marker_ring",
+    "marker_dot",
+    "axis_x",
+    "axis_y",
+    "axis_z",
+    "viewport_hover",
+];
+
+/// The gold of the view cube's hover dot and the machined facet's hover.
+const GOLD: Color32 = Color32::from_rgb(255, 217, 102);
+
+#[test]
+fn the_built_in_columns_keep_the_view_cube_and_marker_colours() {
+    // `ground_ink::cube_ink` before #1120: the dark set, then the light set.
+    let dark = [
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(170),
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(230),
+        Color32::WHITE,
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(160),
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(200),
+        Color32::from_gray(225),
+        Color32::from_gray(240),
+        Color32::WHITE,
+        Color32::from_rgb(245, 70, 70),
+        Color32::from_rgb(60, 220, 80),
+        Color32::from_rgb(90, 140, 255),
+        GOLD,
+    ];
+    let light = [
+        Color32::from_gray(90),
+        Color32::from_gray(20),
+        Color32::from_gray(10),
+        Color32::from_gray(60),
+        Color32::from_gray(60),
+        Color32::from_gray(50),
+        Color32::from_gray(40),
+        Color32::from_gray(20),
+        Color32::from_rgb(215, 20, 20),
+        Color32::from_rgb(0, 140, 30),
+        Color32::from_rgb(20, 70, 230),
+        GOLD,
+    ];
+    assert_eq!(furniture(&Tokens::DARK), dark, "dark column");
+    assert_eq!(furniture(&Tokens::LIGHT), light, "light column");
+}
+
+fn hex(c: Color32) -> String {
+    format!("#{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}", c.r(), c.g(), c.b())
+}
+
+fn parse(base: &str, colors: &str) -> Tokens {
+    let text = format!(
+        r#"{{"format":"camcraft-theme/1","descriptor":{{"name":"g"}},"base":"{base}","colors":{{{colors}}}}}"#
+    );
+    let theme = tf::parse_text(&text, "g.json").unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("the theme reads: {e}"));
+    assert!(theme.notes.is_empty(), "notes: {:?}", theme.notes);
+    theme.tokens
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_view_cube_inks_follow_the_viewport_ground_of_a_theme_file() {
+    // Before #1120 the cube chose its set by the viewport ground. A file
+    // that turns the ground light on the dark base keeps that: each key
+    // it omits takes the light table's value.
+    let light_vp = format!(r#""viewport":"{}""#, hex(Tokens::LIGHT.viewport));
+    assert_eq!(
+        furniture(&parse("dark", &light_vp)),
+        furniture(&Tokens::LIGHT)
+    );
+    let dark_vp = format!(r#""viewport":"{}""#, hex(Tokens::DARK.viewport));
+    assert_eq!(
+        furniture(&parse("light", &dark_vp)),
+        furniture(&Tokens::DARK)
+    );
+    // A ground of the base's own lightness keeps the base's set.
+    let near = format!(
+        r#""viewport":"{}""#,
+        hex(Color32::from_rgb(0x20, 0x22, 0x26))
+    );
+    assert_eq!(furniture(&parse("dark", &near)), furniture(&Tokens::DARK));
+    // A key the file sets wins over the ground's set.
+    let both = format!(r##"{light_vp},"axis_x":"#123456""##);
+    let t = parse("dark", &both);
+    assert_eq!(t.axis_x, Color32::from_rgb(0x12, 0x34, 0x56));
+    assert_eq!(t.axis_y, Tokens::LIGHT.axis_y);
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn each_view_cube_ink_is_a_theme_key() {
+    for name in FURNITURE_KEYS {
+        assert!(
+            tf::COLOR_NAMES.contains(&name),
+            "{name} is a colour key of the theme format"
+        );
+        let t = parse("dark", &format!(r##""{name}":"#0A0B0C""##));
+        let set = furniture(&t);
+        let at = FURNITURE_KEYS
+            .iter()
+            .position(|k| *k == name)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        assert_eq!(
+            set.get(at),
+            Some(&Color32::from_rgb(10, 11, 12)),
+            "{name} sets its own ink"
+        );
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_facet_veil_keeps_the_hover_colour_of_a_semi_transparent_token() {
+    use camcraft_ui::egui_app::ground_ink::facet_veil;
+    // The built-in gold gives the veil it gave before #1120.
+    assert_eq!(
+        facet_veil(GOLD),
+        Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(255, 217, 102, 90)
+    );
+    // The probe of the #3993 review: `#FF000080` gave [45, 0, 0, 90],
+    // because the stored channels are already multiplied by alpha.
+    let half_red = parse("dark", r##""viewport_hover":"#FF000080""##).viewport_hover;
+    assert_eq!(facet_veil(half_red).to_array(), [90, 0, 0, 90]);
+}
+
+/// The overlay inks of a token table, in the order of `OVERLAY_KEYS`.
+fn overlays(t: &Tokens) -> [Color32; 10] {
+    [
+        t.overlay_panel,
+        t.overlay_edge,
+        t.overlay_text,
+        t.overlay_track,
+        t.drop_veil,
+        t.empty_hint,
+        t.pick_halo,
+        t.plate_hole,
+        t.plate_dowel,
+        t.gcode_line,
+    ]
+}
+
+const OVERLAY_KEYS: [&str; 10] = [
+    "overlay_panel",
+    "overlay_edge",
+    "overlay_text",
+    "overlay_track",
+    "drop_veil",
+    "empty_hint",
+    "pick_halo",
+    "plate_hole",
+    "plate_dowel",
+    "gcode_line",
+];
+
+#[test]
+fn the_built_in_columns_keep_the_overlay_colours() {
+    // The literals of `gen_overlay.rs`, `file_drop.rs`, `shell.rs` and
+    // `pick_ink.rs` before #1120, in both columns: these draw sites did
+    // not follow the ground.
+    let before = [
+        Color32::from_black_alpha(200),
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(60),
+        Color32::WHITE,
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(40),
+        Color32::from_black_alpha(140),
+        Color32::from_white_alpha(150),
+        Color32::from_black_alpha(camcraft_ui::pick_ink::HALO_ALPHA),
+        Color32::from_rgb(230, 190, 90),
+        Color32::from_rgb(120, 200, 255),
+        Color32::from_rgb(255, 170, 60),
+    ];
+    assert_eq!(overlays(&Tokens::DARK), before, "dark column");
+    assert_eq!(overlays(&Tokens::LIGHT), before, "light column");
+    // The origin triads' outline reads the handle shadow: the same 170.
+    assert_eq!(Tokens::DARK.handle_shade, Color32::from_black_alpha(170));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn each_overlay_ink_is_a_theme_key() {
+    for (at, name) in OVERLAY_KEYS.iter().enumerate() {
+        assert!(
+            tf::COLOR_NAMES.contains(name),
+            "{name} is a colour key of the theme format"
+        );
+        let t = parse("light", &format!(r##""{name}":"#0A0B0C""##));
+        assert_eq!(
+            overlays(&t)[at],
+            Color32::from_rgb(10, 11, 12),
+            "{name} sets its own ink"
+        );
+    }
+    // A key the file omits keeps its base value; the ground rule of
+    // the view cube inks does not touch the overlays.
+    let dark_vp = format!(r#""viewport":"{}""#, hex(Tokens::DARK.viewport));
+    assert_eq!(
+        overlays(&parse("light", &dark_vp)),
+        overlays(&Tokens::LIGHT)
+    );
+}

+# Record an AI chat replay fixture
+
+Replay tests run offline. Recording is a separate, explicitly authorized QA
+activity. Do not provision a model or send project data to a provider merely
+to run the test suite.
+
+## Record
+
+1. Use a synthetic project without private geometry, credentials or business data.
+2. Save the initial `.camproj`. Record the application commit, platform,
+   provider, model/version, preset, tool mode, system prompt and offered schemas.
+3. Capture each user message and every raw model reply for that turn. Preserve
+   call IDs, content, function names and the original argument strings.
+   Do not repair invalid arguments or convert text into calls.
+4. Save `get_job` after each turn. Record any Allow/Deny decision and each
+   Undo/Redo result. Save another project before starting a fresh chat session.
+5. Keep immutable source links and hashes. Review all files for secrets and
+   private data before publishing. Document any redaction without changing a
+   tool's argument shape. Never use an account key as fixture data.
+
+The q08 source used a separate wire capture because the panel had no export.
+This guide does not authorize traffic capture. Use an approved recording
+method in an isolated QA session; never intercept another person's traffic.
+
+## Make the fixture
+
+Use the format and source mapping in
+[`fixtures/README.md`](../../crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ai_chat/fixtures/README.md).
+Choose complete turns, not only the successful calls. Preserve the original
+reply objects. Keep setup reconstruction separate from recorded output.
+Document why the slice has the same relevant initial state as its source.
+
+Project schemas evolve. Use the normal project loader and explain migrations.
+Update expected values only for a reviewed, intentional change. Do not alter
+raw replies to fit the current parser. Do not preserve an old authorization
+bug by weakening confirmation or refusal expectations.
+
+Project the original job snapshots to stable operation fields. Assert the
+operation count, names, tools, sources and parameters after **each** turn.
+Assert that one Undo reverts the whole mutating turn and one Redo restores it.
+For rejected destructive calls, assert the unchanged document and history.
+Check that refusals appear in the panel and return to the model as errors.
+A model's success text is not evidence that its requested edit succeeded.
+
+## Run and challenge
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib recorded_q08 -- --nocapture
+cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib egui_app::tests::ai_chat
+cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main
+cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings
+```
+
+Add one named test per fixture in the existing `ai_chat` directory suite.
+The transport must consume only its recorded replies and fail on an extra
+round. Never fall back to the HTTP transport or a live model.
+
+Temporarily perturb the test transport's arguments, run the focused test,
+and verify that its document assertion fails. Restore the perturbation and
+run the same test again. Keep both logs outside the source tree. Do not
+commit the perturbation or change production parsing to make the test pass.
+
+These tests check the application workflow. They are not toolpath goldens,
+proof of collision safety, or approval to run a physical machine.

+## #1120 - Colour literals: a guard with exact counts first, then one PR for each family
+
+**What was decided.** The first #1120 PR adds only the guard,
+`crates/ui/tests/theme_files/colour_literals.rs`, with its scanner in
+`colour_scan.rs` beside it. Both are modules of the existing `theme_files`
+test binary (#3187: no new binary), whose gate map names `ui::egui_app`. It walks `crates/ui/src`, counts the
+colour literals in each file that is not a test file, and compares each
+count with a row of `ALLOWED`. A literal is a named constant
+(`Color32::WHITE`) or a constructor whose arguments are all numbers written
+in place; a constructor over variables converts a colour chosen elsewhere
+and does not count. The count must be equal: more fails ("read a
+theme token instead"), fewer also fails ("lower the row"), so the list only
+shrinks. Each row says why: `keep:` for a colour that is not a choice at a
+draw site, `move (#1120 <family>)` for a site that a later PR moves to
+tokens. On `main` at f287a370c the list has 24 files and 142 literals.
+
+The families that later PRs move, each with its tokens and its theme-file
+keys (`theme_files::COLOR_NAMES`):
+- viewport overlays (pick, avoid and handle inks, ground ink, view cube,
+  viewport bar, generate overlay, drop hint, shell overlays);
+- tool drawings (tool, holder and profile previews, tool library views);
+- verdict palettes (`colorvision.rs`), moved into the token table with their
+  values unchanged, as the issue says;
+- G-code syntax colours, window chrome, status inks.
+
+The `keep:` rows are the token tables, the contrast maths, and a colour
+that only measures text.
+
+The guard does not see colour data kept as plain numbers: the G-code syntax
+table in `gcode_highlight.rs` (tuples), and `[u8; 3]` consts such as
+`PICK_RGB8`. The family PRs move those by name, and the last PR checks them
+by hand.
+
+**Why.** On `main` there are about 105 literal sites to move, not the 51 of
+the 2026-11-12 estimate. One PR for all of them would touch about 30 files
+and conflict with most open UI PRs. The guard stops the count from growing
+from the first merge, and each family PR is small and reviewable.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- A guard that only refuses a file with no row. It lets the count inside a
+  listed file grow without notice.
+- Counting every constructor. A first version did: it counted 162, and
+  about 20 of them only convert a palette colour (`from_rgb(r, g, b)`,
+  `from_rgba_unmultiplied(r, g, b, ALPHA)`). Moving those would change
+  nothing a theme can reach.
+- A regex or a parse of the Rust source. A substring search with a small
+  argument scanner is enough for the forms that occur, and the guard stays
+  in `std`. The scanner first removes comments (`//` to the line end and
+  nested `/* */`) and keeps the text of string and char literals: the
+  #3990 review showed that skipping only whole comment lines lets a
+  comment after code hide a literal or add one.
+- A new top-level test binary for the guard. Each `camcraft-ui` test
+  binary costs a link and disk space; the guard is a theme test, so it
+  joins `theme_files`.
+- Moving the colour-vision maths and the contrast maths. They compute
+  colours; they do not choose them.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small. The guard is two test modules. A new literal
+form is one line in `PATTERNS`, and the counts are printed by the failing
+test, ready to paste.
